item.author: Reuters
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Former Japanese prime minister Yasuo Fukuda, who used ⁠his brief period ⁠in office to seek ⁠closer ties with Asian neighbours, particularly China, has died at the age of 90, according to the Nikkei business daily on Monday. The Japanese politician, the first son of a prime minister to become one ‌himself, died on Thursday from heart failure, the Nikkei reported. Becoming prime minister on the sudden resignation of Shinzo Abe for health reasons in 2007, Fukuda lasted less than a year – a tenure...
item.title: Former Japanese prime minister Yasuo Fukuda, known for seeking China ties, dies at 90

item.author: Vivian Au
item.dc:creator: Vivian Au
item.description: Hong Kong is well positioned to help companies deploy green services and technologies across belt and road countries, the city’s leader and a mainland Chinese official have said, with authorities noting that at least five enterprises have signed up. They made the remarks at the Belt and Road Green Innovation Conference, which opened in Hong Kong on Monday. It is the first time the event has been held outside the mainland, as the city seeks to act as a bridge for expanding the global market for...
item.title: Hong Kong positioned as green gateway for belt and road firms: John Lee

item.author: Alcott Wei
item.dc:creator: Alcott Wei
item.description: The Communist Party has started a key four-day conclave focused on party discipline and fighting corruption, as official media outlets say adherence to the party’s leadership under President Xi Jinping is key to the country’s success. The meeting – the fifth plenum of the Communist Party’s 20th Central Committee – began in Beijing on Monday, according to state news agency Xinhua. It said the main agenda for the plenum included a work report by the Politburo to the Central Committee and the...
item.title: China’s Communist Party opens fifth plenum with focus on discipline and loyalty to Xi

item.author: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.dc:creator: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.description: As days of dangerous heat become more frequent in Japan, Sendai has emerged as the most comfortable city, with a climate that is “not too hot and not too cold”. The Miyagi prefectural capital, about 300km (186 miles) from Tokyo, has the best weather, according to the Asahi newspaper, with the lowest number of midsummer and midwinter days among 11 major cities in the nation. Citing Japan Meteorological Agency data, the newspaper reported that Sendai had only 31 midsummer days and no midwinter...
item.title: Cooler than Tokyo: Sendai named Japan’s most comfortable city amid record heat

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: The Saudi-led military coalition said Monday it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by Yemen’s Houthis, after the Iran-backed group claimed a new attack on the international airport in Riyadh. The operation came a day after explosions rattled the Saudi capital and authorities sent text messages to residents warning them of a “hostile aerial threat” targeting the city. The Houthis have carried out waves of strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, including an attack this month...
item.title: Saudi coalition intercepts missile as Houthis claim new attack on Riyadh airport

item.author: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.dc:creator: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.description: Four years ago, party-goers dressed as police officers were reportedly mistaken for the real thing amid a deadly crowd crush in South Korea’s capital. Now, as Seoul prepares for its fourth Halloween since the disaster, police have launched a week-long nationwide crackdown on imitation police uniforms and equipment, aiming to stop any such confusion from happening again. The nationwide operation, announced by the National Police Agency on Sunday, runs until Monday next week. More than 4,500...
item.title: In South Korea, jail time awaits Halloween police impersonators

item.author: Simpson Cheung
item.dc:creator: Simpson Cheung
item.description: A man has died after falling from a building while trying to flee a Hong Kong police raid on a suspected drug den in Yau Ma Tei. The 42-year-old man, surnamed Kwong, was found unconscious outside 385-387 Reclamation Street at about 9.28pm on Sunday. He was rushed to Kwong Wah Hospital, where he was pronounced dead, police said on Monday. At 9.21pm, officers from the Organised Crime and Triad Bureau launched an operation at the building, breaking into a flat suspected of operating as a drug...
item.title: Man falls to death fleeing Hong Kong police raid on suspected drug den

item.author: William Yiu
item.dc:creator: William Yiu
item.description:
A 26-year-old warehouse worker has been injured in Hong Kong after being chased by three dogs and bitten by one of them on his way to work. A source said police received a report at around 8am on Monday from the victim, surnamed Leung, saying one of the dogs pounced on him as he was walking towards his workplace at a logistics company in Yuen Long’s Kam Pok Road. Paramedics arrived at the scene and found the victim with minor wounds. He was sent to Pok Oi Hospital for treatment.
The source said...
item.title: Man bitten after being chased by 3 dogs on his way to work in Yuen Long

item.author: Carol Yang
item.dc:creator: Carol Yang
item.description: An AI-generated Chinese rap song featuring some of the country’s most well-known historical figures has taken social media by storm. Titled “The One Who’s Been There” (Guo Lai Ren), the track crossed 100 million views across platforms in less than two weeks as it tapped into the anxieties of modern life. The song brings together 10 iconic figures from Chinese history and mythology – from revered poets and statesmen to the legendary Monkey King. Rather than reciting classical verses or lecturing...
item.title: 100 million views: why China’s viral AI rap track has struck a chord

item.author: Jess Ma
item.dc:creator: Jess Ma
item.description: An international arbitration body in Hong Kong is exploring business opportunities in the Middle East and Africa, citing the city’s neutrality and predictability as key draws for new markets amid rising geopolitical tensions. Domitille Baizeau, co-chairwoman of the Hong Kong International Arbitration Centre, said the city had benefited from an overall shift in global business growth from Europe to Asia, with overseas businesses increasingly choosing Hong Kong to arbitrate disputes. The...
item.title: Hong Kong arbitration body eyes Mideast, Africa prospects amid global tensions

item.author: Reuters
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Japanese companies are moving to pay compensation to ⁠users following waves ⁠of cyberattacks that have disrupted internet ⁠services and raised concerns about economic stability. GMO Internet said customers would be compensated for losses stemming from unauthorised access following a cyberattack on its foreign exchange trading service, and all customers would receive 5,000 yen (US$32) ‌as “an initial gesture of good faith”, CEO Masatoshi Kumagai said in a blog post on Sunday. The move comes after...
item.title: Japan companies to compensate customers after major cyberattacks

item.author: Ben Jiang,Ann Cao,Richard Chen
item.dc:creator: Ben Jiang,Ann Cao,Richard Chen
item.description: Long before artificial intelligence became the next big thing in the tech industry, Wang Jian was crafting the foundational infrastructure that would eventually power it. In 2008, he joined Alibaba Group Holding – owner of the South China Morning Post – as chief architect and founded Alibaba Cloud in 2009, convincing the company’s leadership to invest heavily in building a cloud computing infrastructure from scratch. Today, Wang’s purview has expanded considerably. As an academician at the...
item.title: Alibaba Cloud founder on how AI can unlock human potential

item.author: Fran Lu
item.dc:creator: Fran Lu
item.description: A Chinese court recently heard a land dispute between neighbours who have been fighting over the same issue for two centuries and across multiple generations, stunning social media users. The court in Yanta district, Xian, in northwestern China’s Shaanxi province, recently presided over a case concerning a land boundary between two neighbouring families, surnamed Du and Zhang. For the past two decades, the neighbours have repeatedly disputed the boundary. When the Dus tried to renovate their...
item.title: Chinese neighbours go viral over 200-year land dispute dating back to Qianlong era

item.author: Chong Ming Lee
item.dc:creator: Chong Ming Lee
item.description: Are China’s increasingly powerful open-weight AI models a cybersecurity threat, or could restricting them ultimately make the internet less secure? The dilemma has become a growing concern as Chinese developers including DeepSeek, Z.ai and Alibaba Group Holding – owner of the South China Morning Post – continue to challenge their American rivals by releasing models that anyone can download, modify and deploy. The growing impact of advanced AI on global cybersecurity has also forced governments...
item.title: Weapon or armour? The contentious debate over China’s open-weight AI

item.author: Victoria Bela
item.dc:creator: Victoria Bela
item.description: Chinese researchers have found that the Yarlung Tsangpo River – soon to host the largest mega dam in the world – may face increased run-off and flood risks over this century. Using tree-ring width chronologies in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, the team reconstructed the river’s run-off history from 1325 to 2020. Along with climate data, this was used to create a model that projected river run-off would increase under future climate scenarios, along with a possible increase in high-run-off...
item.title: Tibetan river hosting world’s biggest dam is facing increasing flood risk: study

item.author: Bloomberg
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: Singapore has expanded its investigation into haze-creating fires in Indonesia that have blanketed the city state in smog, requesting information from 10 locally registered companies. The National Environment Agency (NEA) sent notices seeking documents and details of land concessions in Indonesia owned by the firms, their firefighting and blaze prevention measures, and their relationship to other relevant companies, according to a Friday statement. All 10 Singapore-registered companies were...
item.title: Singapore’s toxic haze probe expands to 10 palm oil, forestry firms

item.author: Emily Hung
item.dc:creator: Emily Hung
item.description: The head of Hong Kong’s new drug regulatory body has pledged to build a fully capable and globally trusted agency that will become a catalyst for medical innovation rather than merely acting as a “miniature version” of existing overseas models. Dr Li Zili, controller of the Hong Kong Centre for Medical Products Regulation (CMPR), said that while many other places in Asia, such as mainland China, Singapore and Japan, had established regulatory agencies long ago, Hong Kong had a distinctive...
item.title: Head of Hong Kong’s new drug regulator pledges to build trust, push innovation

item.author: Wanxin Li
item.dc:creator: Wanxin Li
item.description: The latest rankings confirm what many in Hong Kong already know: the city’s universities are exceptional. Five institutions continue to sit among the world’s top 100, reflecting decades of investment, academic ambition and hard work. Yet behind the rankings triumph lies a question that receives far less attention: what happens to the people responsible for that success? As universities compete ever harder for rankings, grants and prestige, academics face growing pressure to produce results on...
item.title: Hong Kong’s pursuit of top university rankings comes at a cost

item.author: Minxiao Chang
item.dc:creator: Minxiao Chang
item.description: While few dispute that China is narrowing the gap with the United States in developing artificial intelligence (AI) models, there is one area where Chinese firms are already the undisputed leaders: video. China has seen a proliferation of advanced generative AI video models – systems trained on visual data to generate or edit video content based on user inputs such as text prompts, images and audio. The country’s vast short-video ecosystems and looser copyright rules have helped give Chinese...
item.title: China shoots ahead on AI video models

item.author: Zoe SL Chan
item.dc:creator: Zoe SL Chan
item.description: Hong Kong’s insurance watchdog is tightening oversight of the city’s booming premium financing market, as the once-niche lending arrangement spreads to lower-tier insurance buyers, while also reviewing regulations, particularly on how insurers evaluate clients’ affordability, according to Insurance Authority executives. Premium financing allows policyholders to borrow money from financial institutions to pay upfront premiums on large life insurance policies, which are commonly used as a wealth...
item.title: Hong Kong to tighten burgeoning premium financing market as red flags, risks emerge

item.author: William Zheng
item.dc:creator: William Zheng
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s tour of a commercial vehicle factory during a surprise visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday points to Pyongyang’s drive to modernise its buses and expand industrial ties with Beijing. In a symbolic move, Kim crossed into China via the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge on Saturday and also returned to North Korea via the bridge later in the day. It was Kim’s first trip to China since he attended a military parade in Beijing last September. His...
item.title: Why North Korean leader Kim Jong-un toured a Chinese bus factory in Dandong

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: North Korea sent a letter to the United Nations Security Council accusing Seoul of fabricating a landmine explosion that injured three South Korean soldiers, its state media reported on Monday. Tensions between the two Koreas have soared since the South last month blamed the blast inside the heavily fortified demilitarised zone that separates the countries on landmines laid by the North, an accusation it has fiercely rejected. The North Korean permanent representative to the UN sent a letter on...
item.title: North Korea tells UN South ‘fabricated’ border landmine blast

item.author: Igor Patrick
item.dc:creator: Igor Patrick
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won re-election on Sunday in a dramatic comeback after trailing in the first round, extending the rule of a government that has overseen record Chinese investment. The Superior Electoral Court said Lula had 51.79 per cent of valid votes against 48.21 per cent for right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, with 99.99 per cent votes counted. No candidate who trailed after the first round had won a run-off since Brazil adopted the system in 1989. Addressing...
item.title: Lula pulls off Brazil’s first-ever run-off comeback to beat Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro

item.author: Jess Ma
item.dc:creator: Jess Ma
item.description: Interpol will seek approval at its general assembly in Hong Kong next month for a new “silver notice” system to target criminals’ assets and speed up financial investigations into transnational crime. Hong Kong’s police chief also pledged to make financial investigations and scams a top priority in discussions with overseas counterparts during Interpol’s annual meeting, which the city is hosting for the first time. Interpol secretary general Valdecy Urquiza said in an interview in Hong Kong that...
item.title: Interpol’s Hong Kong meeting to consider ‘silver notice’ targeting criminal assets

item.dc:creator: David D. Lee
item.description: “How can South Korea’s law be this weak? Twenty-three people died!” Those were the words of Chinese mother Li Shun-ji after South Korea’s Supreme Court upheld a reduced four-year prison sentence for Aricell CEO Park Soon-kwan last Tuesday over a 2024 factory fire that killed 23 workers, including Li’s then-24-year-old daughter, Yan Jing-jing. The blaze at the lithium battery manufacturer’s factory in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi province, killed 17 Chinese nationals, one Laotian national and five South...

item.title: Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint plans retail stablecoin as HSBC RedCoin launches

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: US President President Donald Trump at a Sunday campaign rally ratcheted up his push to link US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed to Muslim extremists, comparing him to the 9/11 attackers while saying Democrats would let violent anti-American terrorists into the United States. “I’m here to keep a jihadist, Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator,” the president told a receptive audience in Port Huron, which is in a Michigan area where 66 per cent of the vote went to Trump...

item.author: Alice Wu
item.dc:creator: Alice Wu
item.description: It’s common knowledge that Hong Kong has a spectacular skyline, especially at night. And given our current obsession with boosting tourism and other value-adding objectives, it shouldn’t come as a surprise that our tourism authorities are actively adding more light to our night skyline. The Tourism Board tried holding monthly firework and drone shows in 2024, but had to scale back after a budget cut – and amid questions of whether more frequent displays, costing the public HK$1 million...

item.author: Igor Patrick
item.dc:creator: Igor Patrick
item.description: A Supreme Court justice in Brazil ordered polls in the presidential run-off to stay open for two more hours on Sunday, minutes after voting had officially ended at 5pm Brasilia time (4am on Monday in Hong Kong). The order left election officials across China’s biggest trading partner in Latin America unsure whether to reopen polling stations or send their machines to be counted. Justice Cristiano Zanin, who was President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s lawyer before joining the court in 2023, acted...
item.title: Brazil’s election left hanging as judge extends vote after polls close, sparking chaos

item.author: Associated Press
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: The presidential election in Bulgaria on Sunday ended inconclusively, with the next head of state to be picked in a run-off, according to election officials. A record low turnout, attributed by observers to a general mistrust in politicians resulting in voter apathy, will pit two contrasting political visions against each other in a highly polarised contest on November 1. In a surprisingly strong performance, the candidate of the pro-Western reformist opposition, Andrey Gyurov, will face the...
item.title: Bulgaria presidential vote heads to run-off between incumbent and pro-West rival

item.author: Reuters
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Venezuelan opposition ⁠leader Maria Corina Machado was greeted by tens of thousands of cheering supporters as she made ⁠her way by car to Caracas on Sunday night, after she arrived home following several failed return attempts which have strained her ties with US President Donald Trump’s administration. “This country is giving lessons to everyone,” she shouted as her convoy entered the capital, leaning out of the sunroof to shake hands and hug raucous supporters Nobel Peace Prize laureate...
item.title: Machado makes dramatic return to Venezuela after nearly a year in exile

item.author: Associated Press
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: US Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday defended the Trump administration’s lawsuit to block certification of Alaska’s Senate results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses the race and argued that the legal challenge was a necessary step to avoid confusing voters in the closely watched midterm race. US President Donald Trump, who said on Friday that he was “the one that said do it”, is not trying to overturn state election results “in any way, shape or form” on the cusp of the November 3...
item.title: US attorney general denies Trump meddling with Alaska Senate race lawsuit

item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Marine Le Pen, France’s far-right candidate to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, kicked off her campaign Sunday vowing to “restore the rule of law” if elected next year. Le Pen – the front runner in the polls – seems to be benefiting from the convulsions France has been going through for weeks, which have seen violence flare on the sidelines of mass cost-of-living rallies. “We are going to restore the rule of law,” she said, after looting and arson erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations...
item.title: Le Pen launches presidential bid amid French unrest, vows to ‘restore rule of law’

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Iran and its allies might try to disrupt Tuesday’s Israeli elections, warning the Islamic republic against any hostile acts. The remarks came as Israel’s Channel 12 reported, citing unnamed sources, that there had been a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the prime minister denied. Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, touting the war he...
item.title: Netanyahu warns Iran may try to disrupt Israel election: ‘don’t test us’

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Storms battered northern Europe Sunday, killing a man, cutting power to more than 150,000 homes and disrupting travel and phone networks. A man died when a tree fell on him in southwestern Scotland, while a runner in a marathon in northern France was injured when a tree was felled by strong winds during the race. More than 82,000 homes in Britain, nearly 60,000 in France and at least 10,000 in Germany had power cuts inflicted by the passage of storms Boelo and Austen within 24 hours of each...
item.title: Storms batter northern Europe, grounding flights and cutting power

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Philippine police are investigating a laptop found alongside images of child abuse at the former home of Meghan Markle’s estranged father, with “full results” expected in a week, the country’s interior minister told reporters. Thomas Markle, whose daughter is married to Britain’s Prince Harry, had been living in Cebu in the Philippines until reportedly returning to the US earlier this year. Philippine interior minister Jonvic Remulla said the country planned to take “appropriate legal actions”...
item.title: Philippines plan ‘appropriate legal action’ against Thomas Markle

item.author: Danny Mok
item.dc:creator: Danny Mok
item.description: A traveller was injured after a power bank overheated and emitted smoke aboard an HK Express flight from Hong Kong to South Korea on Sunday, prompting crew members to deploy emergency safety measures before the aircraft landed safely. The incident occurred on flight UO676 to Jeju, which was carrying 236 passengers and seven crew, prompting an apology from HK Express. The budget airline, a subsidiary of Hong Kong flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways, said the power bank was stored in a bag under a...
item.title: HK Express passenger injured after power bank overheats on flight to Jeju

item.author: Gabriel Dominguez
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Dominguez
item.description: With China flexing its naval power across the Pacific and bilateral tensions running high, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is weighing a move long viewed as taboo – nuclear-powered submarines for the Maritime Self-Defence Force fleet. “We will seriously consider [the possibility] in a concrete and realistic manner,” Takaichi told the Japanese parliament on October 14. Yet with Tokyo set to revise its core security documents by year’s end, the proposal is dividing the ruling coalition. The...
item.title: Eye on China: Japan reopens taboo debate over nuclear-powered submarines

item.author: Kristen Cheung
item.dc:creator: Kristen Cheung
item.description: Hong Kong’s No 2 official has pledged to open extra clearance counters and vehicle lanes at the recently revamped Huanggang Port control point ahead of peak hours, after Halloween crowds and concertgoers created heavy cross-border congestion. Chief Secretary Eric Chan Kwok-ki, who inspected the Shenzhen Bay and Huanggang ports on Sunday, said he had instructed the Security Bureau to step up advance assessments and passenger flow forecasting. He added that he had directed the Transport and...
item.title: Hong Kong to boost Huanggang Port capacity after Halloween, concert congestion

item.author: Laura Zhou
item.dc:creator: Laura Zhou
item.description: The debate over ethnic identity in Xinjiang has triggered an online clash between Chinese and Turkish social media users. The row began earlier this month when a Turkish social media user recalled an encounter with a Uygur from Xinjiang, the region in China that is home to nearly 12 million mainly Muslim Turkic speakers. The user wrote that the woman did not look Chinese, but when asked whether she considered herself Turkic, the woman responded: “No, I’m Chinese.” The user also called on her to...
item.title: War of words over Xinjiang erupts between Chinese and Turkish social media users

item.author: Edith Lin
item.dc:creator: Edith Lin
item.description: The death of veteran Hong Kong stock market commentator Louie Shum Chun-ying has drawn public attention to heart disease, after a police source revealed he had a history of the condition as well as diabetes. Heart disease was one of the leading causes of death in Hong Kong, with more than 6,500 fatalities recorded in 2024, according to the Department of Health. While residents at risk should monitor their health and seek timely medical care, a local cardiologist stressed that bystanders could...
item.title: Louie Shum’s death: heart disease in Hong Kong and what to do in an emergency

item.author: Alex Lo
item.dc:creator: Alex Lo
item.description: In the early days of the student protests in France, mainstream Western media took the protesters’ claims about poor school facilities and declining resources at face value. Only when the violence spread across the country, and to some of its European neighbours, did people begin to ask whether deeper causes were at play. Leftists blame social problems, from the cost-of-living pressures linked to the war in Ukraine to rising unemployment, especially among the young. Right-wing critics blame...
item.title: The West’s double standard on global unrest

item.author: Albee Zhang
item.dc:creator: Albee Zhang
item.description: China’s Liaoning aircraft carrier strike group sailed beyond the first island chain last week to reach the southernmost waters of the Philippines, suggesting an intent to position itself closer to ongoing US-Japan joint exercises. Philippine news channel BNC reported that the carrier group reached about 25 nautical miles (46km) east-southeast of Balut Island, the southernmost point of the Philippines, before sailing northeast on Friday. That positioned the warships past the first island chain, a...
item.title: China’s Liaoning carrier and USS Theodore Roosevelt may be in Philippine Sea at same time

item.dc:creator: Kyodo
item.description: Prosecutors indicted a 20-year-old US Marine on Sunday on suspicion of robbing and murdering a woman in Okinawa earlier this month as the case renews anti-base sentiment among locals burdened with hosting the bulk of US military installations in Japan. Devin Ballard, who is stationed at Futenma Air Base, is charged with killing the woman by wrapping a phone cord around her neck at a hotel in Naha, the capital of the southern island prefecture, and taking her backpack containing a wallet on...

item.description: In the second of a four-part Health Matters wellness series on frontier medicine in Hong Kong, Fiona Sun looks into how a new PCR system can detect cancer, infections and birth defects within hours, and what it will take to bring such laboratory breakthroughs to patients. item.description: A pivotal trial of vaccines against the strain of Ebola that is driving a deadly outbreak across parts of Africa has begun in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where the epidemic originated and the vast majority of cases and deaths have occurred. The first participant was vaccinated on Friday in Bunia, eastern DR Congo, with Merck & Co’s Ervebo shot, which has been approved to guard against a different Ebola species. item.description: Hong Kong firefighters battled for five hours to bring a hill fire near a residential area in Tuen Mun under control on Sunday, with a government helicopter sent to help bring the flames under control.
